name: Eliashib
overview: Eliashib was a male Levite, identified as the eleventh-chosen priest among the twenty-four priestly courses established in Israel. He belonged to the line of Eleazar, one of the sons of Aaron, which situates him within the hereditary priesthood. His role as a priest in this structured division emphasizes his service in the temple worship system.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliashib means 'G-d restores,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning centered on divine restoration. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 24:12, highlights the spiritual significance attributed to his identity within Israel's priestly tradition.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Eliashib as a descendant of Eleazar, linking him to a prominent priestly lineage. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are detailed in the biblical text concerning him.
scriptureSignificance: Eliashib's significance lies in his appointment as the eleventh priestly leader among the twenty-four courses, a system instituted to organize temple service and worship under God's covenant. His placement in the line of Eleazar underscores the continuity of priestly duties passed through generations, reflecting God's orderly provision for worship. His role contributes to the understanding of the structured priesthood essential for Israel's spiritual life.
